CVE-2026-115701.title: Cowboy HTTP/1.1 Unbounded Buffering of Pipelined Data During Request Handling Enables Memory Exhaustion
CVE-2026-115701.description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowboy allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust connection process memory over HTTP/1.1.

Once a request has been received in full and its handler is still running, cowboy_http:parse/2 in src/cowboy_http.erl appends every further byte that arrives on the keep-alive connection to the connection buffer and returns to the receive loop without parsing it. The socket stays in active mode and no limit applies to this buffer: max_request_line_length, max_headers and the other parser limits only take effect once the handler returns and parsing resumes, and the only timer in this state is idle_timeout (default 60 seconds), which is reset on every received chunk. A client can therefore send an arbitrary amount of data on one connection for as long as the handler runs, and a few connections to an endpoint that holds requests open can drive the Erlang VM into out-of-memory conditions.

CVE-2026-116252.title: pgAdmin 4: Materialized view refresh redirects its connection through a crafted database name
CVE-2026-116252.description:
pgAdmin 4's materialized view refresh passed the target database's name to psql's --dbname argument unchanged. libpq treats a --dbname value containing "=" (or a postgresql:// URI) as a full connection string, whose keywords override the host, port and other settings pgAdmin had supplied. A database whose name is such a string, which any role with CREATEDB can create, therefore redirected the psql process pgAdmin starts for the refresh to a host and port of the creator's choosing, and the connecting user's saved server password was presented to that endpoint. It also let the pgAdmin host be made to open connections to arbitrary addresses.

The same weakness was fixed for Backup, Restore, Maintenance and Import/Export Data in earlier releases (CVE-2026-86862); the materialized view refresh was the remaining caller. The fix routes the name through the same database_conninfo() helper, so libpq treats it strictly as a database name.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

CVE-2026-118988.title: CallBackery versions before 0.60.1 for Perl let unauthenticated clients read the POD of any file via path traversal in the /doc route
CVE-2026-118988.description:
CallBackery versions before 0.60.1 for Perl let unauthenticated clients read the POD of any file via path traversal in the /doc route.

Every CallBackery application mounts its documentation plugin at /doc, ahead of any session check. The route passes the requested name to Pod::Simple::Search->find without validation. find splits the name on "::" and joins the parts into a file path, so a name such as "..::..::..::etc::motd" escapes @INC.

Any file the server process can read is reachable. Only POD is rendered, but a file with a POD directive and no "=cut" is POD to the end of the file.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could cause Splunk SOAR to send the stored root credential for an external credential store to a host that the user controls. Depending on the configuration, the exposed credential could include an access token, application secret, account password, or client certificate.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR reuses the stored credential when the user changes the external credential store endpoint without supplying replacement credentials.

CVE-2026-81815.title: Apache OFBiz: SQL injection - performFind ignore-case values, MySQL/MariaDB
CVE-2026-81815.description: SQL Injection in the entity engine's generic performFind service in Apache OFBiz 24.09 before 24.09.08 on MySQL/MariaDB-backed deployments allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to disclose arbitrary rows from the queried entity by submitting an ignore-case find request (e.g. _ic=Y) with a crafted value, causing SqlJdbcUtil.addValueSingle to inline the EntityFunction-wrapped value directly into the SQL text using ANSI-only single-quote doubling instead of binding it as a parameter, which is insufficient on MySQL/MariaDB because those dialects also honor backslash escapes, letting a backslash-terminated payload break out of the string literal and turn the WHERE clause into a tautology. The default Derby datasource and PostgreSQL are not affected because they do not interpret backslash as an escape character in this context. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 24.09.08, which fixes this issue.

CVE-2026-99281.title: tun: Require CAP_NET_ADMIN to attach to an ownerless device
CVE-2026-99281.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tun: Require CAP_NET_ADMIN to attach to an ownerless device

Twenty years ago I made creating a tuntap device require CAP_NET_ADMIN
in commit ca6bb5d7ab22 ("[NET]: Require CAP_NET_ADMIN to create tuntap
devices.")

The idea was to allow the permissions on /dev/net/tun to be relaxed to
0666 and thus allow owners of tun devices assigned with TUNSETOWNER to
actually open it and get at their devices.

What we missed at the time was that persistent devices with *no* owner
were already essentially world-consumable, and anyone who could open
the device node could also attach to those.

Even then, using persistent devices with no explicitly set owner — on
the (false) presumption that CAP_NET_ADMIN would be required to open
them — wasn't an egregious userspace bug. There are cases where it does
make sense to separate the creation/configuration of the netdevice, from
the process which shovels packets into it.

Since then,…

CVE-2026-99515.title: iommufd: Fix event queue release use-after-free
CVE-2026-99515.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommufd: Fix event queue release use-after-free

iommufd_eventq_fops_release() drops the file's users reference before
reading eventq->ictx. Once that reference is dropped, IOMMU_DESTROY in
another thread can remove and free the event queue, so the later load
accesses freed memory.

Read ictx while the users reference still pins the event queue, then
drop the reference and put the saved context. The context reference
taken by iommufd_eventq_init() keeps ictx valid until the put. Fault and
vEVENTQ file descriptors share this release path.

CVE-2026-99704.title: mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares
CVE-2026-99704.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares

The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are scaled to parts per million, but
the threshold and ratio operands are unsigned long. On 32-bit kernels,
their multiplication can wrap before the result is assigned to u64.

For example, with a threshold of 25600 pages and the default maximum ratio
of 1000000, wb_max_thresh becomes 4125 pages instead of 25600. The shared
threshold and minimum share calculations can overflow in the same way,
producing incorrect per-writeback dirty limits.

Use a u64 threshold for the three ratio multiplications and div_u64() to
retain the existing division order and rounding.

CVE-2026-99793.title: Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests
CVE-2026-99793.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: L2CAP: Only accept connection responses to outstanding requests

An outgoing channel waits in BT_CONNECT until security
and the feature mask exchange complete, and only then
sends its connection request. A peer can answer it
before that with a connection response matching our
source CID. The channel then moves to BT_CONFIG,
completes configuration and becomes connected before
security has completed. If security then fails,
l2cap_security_cfm() leaves the connected channel
alone, so it stays up on a link that did not reach
the required security level.

A connection response with a zero source CID is
matched by identifier. Another channel can hold the
same identifier for a response it still has to send,
so the lookup can pick the wrong channel.

Only accept a connection response while our request
is outstanding, and only look at such channels when
matching by identifier.
